Ukraine: Kharkiv apartment block hit by Russian strike, 25 injured Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 28/09/2026 - 12:30 GMT+2 A Russian strike hit a nine-storey apartment block in Kharkiv early on Monday, injuring 25 people, including nine children. Emergency workers evacuated 32 residents from the damaged building, according to regional authorities. … More The attack struck the Saltivskyi district at about 4am , destroying apartments on the lower floors. Emergency crews rescued 32 people from the building and searched the damaged floors for anyone still trapped inside. ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT The injured children were aged between three and 15 . Two boys, aged eight and 12, were taken to hospital, while the others received treatment at the scene. Several victims were also treated for injuries and acute stress reactions. Rescue workers, police and medical teams continued clearing debris on Monday. Authorities said investigators were trying to determine which weapon had been used. The strike came during a wider wave of Russian overnight attacks. Four people were injured in Kyiv , while preliminary reports indicated that two others were hurt in Odesa. The attack is the latest to hit Kharkiv , a major city in north-eastern Ukraine that has faced repeated Russian strikes since the full-scale invasion began. https://bnn-news.com/social/we-cannot-ru.text: Director of Latvia’s Constitution Protection Bureau Egils Zviedris. · Photo: Ieva Leini;sa/LETA Advertisements SAB has been warning about the escalation of Russia’s unconventional warfare since early spring. According to Zviedris, Russia has been unable to achieve its stated objective of victory in the war against Ukraine and is therefore escalating the situation in Europe in response to Western support for Ukraine. This escalation includes hybrid threats such as cyberattacks, physical acts of sabotage and information warfare. Russia is escalating the situation because it has failed to weaken Western support for Ukraine or secure an easing of sanctions, Zviedris explained. This has resulted in incidents such as drones carrying explosives at Leipzig Airport and acts of sabotage targeting railway lines in European countries. “Russia is raising the stakes, and unfortunately, we cannot rule out civilian casualties,” the head of Latvia’s intelligence service stressed. Advertisements Zviedris pointed out that, so far, false-flag operations are essentially the only type of operation Russia has not carried out in Europe, as other forms of hostile activity have already occurred. He recalled that Latvia has experienced the desecration of monuments and an arson attack on the Museum of the Occupation of Latvia, while Russian opposition figures living in Lithuania have been attacked. Recent warnings by Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk about threats from Russia were specifically related to the risk of false-flag operations, Zviedris said. He also pointed to a recent Russian attack on a Ukrainian passenger train just two kilometres from the Polish border. “Tusk was therefore warning about Russian attacks near the borders of NATO countries. Such statements are a warning to Russia that we see what it is doing near the borders of our countries and that we will not tolerate it,” the SAB director added. Advertisements Zviedris also recalled that Latvia has requested the deployment of four NATO fighter jets to the country for the duration of the Saeima election, a request to which Germany has responded. The move is intended to prevent possible provocations, such as unidentified flying objects entering Latvian airspace, which could subsequently fuel speculation about the legitimacy of the election process. “So the threat from Russia is real, and as the aggressor is unable to achieve its objectives in Ukraine, the stakes are being raised,” Zviedris added. Photograph: Ammar Awad/Reuters West Bank Israeli settlers attack olive farmers and Washington Post journalist in West Bank Settlers hurl rocks at Palestinians and beat photographer Heidi Levine as part of yearly attacks to disrupt harvest William Christou Fri 16 Oct 2026 10.06 EDT Last modified on Fri 16 Oct 2026 10.20 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Israeli settlers have attacked Palestinians across the occupied West Bank in a coordinated movement to disrupt the annual olive harvest, burning cars and trees and injuring Palestinians and a Washington Post photographer. Masked settlers wielding clubs and other weapons attacked people attempting to harvest their olives in towns across the West Bank on Friday. At least six people were injured in the town of Abu Falah near Ramallah, the Palestinian Red Crescent Society said. At least 80 settlers, some of whom were carrying firearms or clubs, gathered to stop Palestinians from harvesting their olives in Abu Falah, using slingshots to hurl rocks at the farmers in view of Israeli military vehicles. When some of the Palestinians then picked up rocks to defend themselves, the Israeli military fired teargas in their direction. View image in fullscreen Teargas fired by Israeli forces. Photograph: Léo Corrêa/AP The Israeli Foreign Press Association said in a statement: “This is the latest in a long line of violent attacks by Israeli settlers against journalists and other civilians in the occupied West Bank. Yet our repeated calls for action to confront this lawlessness have been ignored by Israeli authorities.” Among those injured was the Washington Post photographer Heidi Levine, who was beaten by settlers in an attack that lasted more than 10 minutes, according to witnesses. Settlers stole her passport, phone, wallet and equipment. “I was attacked, pushed to the ground. Luckily, I had my flak jacket and helmet, otherwise I probably wouldn’t even be here, because they just kept kicking and kicking me,” Levine said from a hospital bed in Ramallah. She said the attack ended when her Palestinian colleagues intervened to save her. In a statement, the Washington Post said Levine had been wearing visible markings clearly identifying her as a journalist. View image in fullscreen Levine speaking to journalists in hospital after the attack. Photograph: Ali Sawafta/Reuters There has been a surge of settler violence against Palestinians over the past month. Settlers have carried out at least 170 attacks since 27 September, around the start of the annual olive harvest, according to Yesh Din, an Israeli rights group. Every year, settlers attack Palestinians trying to harvest their olives, but this year’s harvest has seen an uptick in violence as Israel’s elections approach at the end of October. At least four Palestinians have been killed and more than 100 others have been injured over the past month, Palestinian authorities said. Thousands of trees have been damaged. Israel imposed new rules on the olive harvest this year, barring Palestinians from harvesting their trees located in Area C – an area under the Israeli military’s control, which comprises most of the West Bank’s agricultural land. View image in fullscreen Palestinians and activists collecting olives after the attack on Friday. Photograph: Léo Corrêa/AP The new orders prohibit Palestinians from entering about 8,800 hectares (21,800 acres) of agricultural land – a 30% increase from the year prior – without approval of the Israeli military. By contrast, the military gave Israeli citizens access to more land this year. ‘They have total impunity’: West Bank settler violence surges after Gaza ceasefire Read more The rights group Peace Now says the military decreased the amount of land Israeli citizens were prohibited from entering from about 1,070 hectares in 2025 to 680 hectares in 2026, for the purpose of preventing settler violence. The olive harvest is an economic lifeline for Palestinians and has grown in importance since Israel revoked work permits for many Palestinians in the West Bank after the Hamas-led attack on 7 October 2023. Photos and videos showed large swathes of agricultural land with uprooted olive trees in Kufur Malek, outside Ramallah, where Israeli bulldozers had razed trees. Settlers rarely face accountability for their violence, even when well documented. Rights groups say settlers enjoy the protection of the Israeli military, which intervenes only if Palestinians try to defend themselves. View image in fullscreen Israeli soldiers move towards a Palestinian man lying wounded on the road after they shot him during the settler attack. Photograph: Léo Corrêa/AP The Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, has on occasion condemned the violence, which he says is due to just about 100 settlers, but he has taken few steps to stop settler violence. Settlements have rapidly expanded across the West Bank under his rightwing government, leading to international condemnation. The UN and most countries judge settlements to be in violation of international law. Friday’s attack in Abu Falah followed a similar attack hours earlier near the West Bank village of Turmus Ayya, where settlers burned three cars after attacking Palestinians harvesting olives. Videos shared by the Israeli rights group B’tselem showed hundreds of bags of olives “violently” stolen by Israeli settlers from Palestinians and taken to Israeli olive presses. Sarit Michaeli, an independent activist, said settlers were stealing Palestinians’ olive crop on a scale “never seen before in my 22-year history of working on this issue”. A spokesperson for the US embassy in Jerusalem said it was aware of reports of the attack and declined to comment further due to privacy laws. Photograph: MEGA/GC Images US news Thomas Markle, Meghan’s father, jailed after cutting off ankle monitor, DoJ says Estranged father of Duchess of Sussex was arrested for keeping child sexual abuse material, authorities say Maya Yang and agencies Tue 10 Nov 2026 17.37 EST First published on Tue 10 Nov 2026 15.08 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The estranged father of Meghan Markle, the Duchess of Sussex, has been jailed after US authorities said he cut an electronic monitoring device off his ankle, days after his arrest for keeping child sexual abuse material in storage units in California . Thomas Markle, 82, was in custody awaiting a hearing in federal court in Tampa, Florida, first assistant US attorney Bill Essayli said. He was arrested shortly after he cut off the ankle bracelet at 1.45am on Tuesday, Essayli said. “Release conditions are court orders, not suggestions. We are asking the court to revoke his release and detain him pending trial, and we will continue to prosecute this case to the fullest extent of the law,” Essayli said. The US magistrate judge Lindsay Griffin agreed on Tuesday that Markle now must be kept in custody. Markle’s arrest on Friday followed the seizure of approximately 78 items, including slides, film negatives and books that contained suspected child sexual abuse images in storage in the Los Angeles area, Essayli said. Among the alleged child sexual abuse material were sexually explicit photographs of Markle with underage girls, including one taken in what appears to be part of a motel chain in the Philippines, Reuters reports. According to the criminal complaint, the special agent investigating Markle’s alleged storage unit said he “viewed a collection of what appeared to be strips of 35mm film negatives seized from Storage Unit 1 registered to Markle”. “To date, I have identified approximately 18 images that appeared to constitute child pornography,” the special agent noted in the complaint, adding that the investigation remains ongoing. Markle reportedly had rented the storage units in Los Angeles since 2008, with the FBI noting that the most recent auto-payment for the units was on 14 October. “Markle’s use of Storage Unit 1 was also corroborated by items found within the unit bearing his name, including boxes labeled ‘Tom Markle’ and an address within the central district of California,” the criminal complaint said. During his arrest last week, he was taken from a senior care center in Lakeland, Florida, by ambulance. Hours later, a judge allowed Markle to be released on the condition that he be electronically monitored, which typically means wearing an ankle tether. According to Griffin, Markle’s court appearance last Friday included a “lack of recall”. Griffin also cited Markle’s “health condition” and “advanced age” as part of his appearance. The judge ordered a mental competency exam and a report by 20 November. Griffin said she found “reasonable cause to believe” Markle was suffering from a condition “rendering him mentally incompetent to the extent that he is unable to understand the nature and consequences of the proceedings against him or to assist properly in his defense”, CBS reported . His daughter, Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex , married Prince Harry at Windsor Castle in 2018. They have two children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet. She is an American citizen and actor who starred in the US television drama Suits. Meghan recently said she was “deeply distressed” by allegations that a collection of child sexual abuse images had been found at her father’s former home. She also revealed that a letter containing “troubling allegations” about him had been sent to police in London in 2019. “It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated,” Meghan said of the letter. “I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications’ distortion over the years, any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children was for one reason: to protect them.” Thomas Markle was living in the Philippines this year when he suffered a stroke and had his left leg amputated. That forced him to return to the US. His arrest followed reports by the Sun, a British tabloid newspaper, that Meghan’s half-brother found a collection of child sexual abuse images while clearing out their father’s home in the Philippines. That discovery led to information about two US storage units in California, which Markle had rented since 2008.
